correctness.rationale: Tran's affine-coordinate identities give the component of \(n_i-n_j\) along \(M_j-M_i\), while his normal-vector identity gives its full norm. Their difference is exactly \((q-1)^2\varepsilon_{ij}\). The other \(n-1\) vertices of a regular \(n\)-simplex, measured from the midpoint of \(M_iM_j\), form a basis of the perpendicular bisector with Gram matrix \(L^2(2I+J)/4\). Inverting that matrix converts the perpendicular normal component exactly into the claimed quadratic form. The scale-parameter and pointwise row estimates then follow from the source's orthogonal-projection inequality and Cauchy--Schwarz. All quantifiers and the endpoint \(\varepsilon_{ij}=0\) were checked explicitly.

value.rationale: Reflection defects are a central device in the source's open symmetry questions: exact zeros certify hyperplane reflections and strict positivity excludes them. The new identity upgrades that binary test to an exact metric distance from the transposition-symmetry locus in the natural weighted row coordinates. Its explicit square-root estimates can be used to quantify near-reflections in numerical or interval searches and clarify how the source's zero-defect argument degenerates. This is a structural lemma tied directly to the source's main symmetry mechanism rather than an arbitrary parameter computation.
